worldattribute-complexnutritionStart-des: How full a new character's calorie reserve is when they first spawn. The reserve's size follows the diet tier a character starts on: 6 days on Getting By, so Normal gives 3 days (Brutal starts on Malnourished with 2 days, and Rock Bottom on Starving with 1 day). It only applies the first time a character joins the world; Respawn effects: Calories/Diet Tier sets what happens to it when they die.
worldconfig-complexnutritionStart-RockBo: Rock Bottom: an almost empty calorie reserve (good luck!)
worldattribute-complexnutritionStartStor: How full a new character's vitamin, mineral and fiber stores are when they first spawn. Vitamins A, D, E and K and the minerals hold 20 days, so Normal gives 10 days of each. Vitamin C, the B vitamins and fiber hold 2 days, so Normal gives 1 day.
worldconfig-complexnutritionStartStores-: Rock Bottom: almost empty stores (good luck!)
worldattribute-complexnutritionRespawnCa: What dying does to a character's calorie reserve and diet tier. Lose calories on death leaves a tenth of what it held, but never less than 1,000kcal. Keep calories on death leaves it as it was. Reset calorie progress on death leaves 1,000kcal, or almost nothing on a Rock Bottom start, and sends a character's diet back to the tier a new character starts on (never up). Lose one diet tier on death loses calories as Lose calories on death does, and drops the diet one tier. The gut always empties on death.
worldconfig-complexnutritionRespawnCalor: Reset calorie progress on death (for masochists only!)
Lose one diet tier on death
worldattribute-complexnutritionKeepStore: Keep vitamin and mineral reserves on death

When on, a character keeps their vitamin, mineral and fiber stores when they die, and their vitamin C and B vitamin day counts carry on. When off, those stores go back to what Starting vitamin and mineral reserves gives a new character. The gut always empties on death.
worldattribute-complexnutritionAdvancedD: Shows more detail when you hover over the Carbs, Fats and Protein bars: how many calories the food being digested will give, how long it will take and how fast it is being absorbed. This is the default: each player can change it for themselves in the settings menu.
worldattribute-complexnutritionMeatInPot: Lets raw, cooked and cured poultry and bushmeat go into meat stews and soups as regular ingredients. Changing it takes effect the next time the world is loaded.
worldattribute-complexnutritionDiscover-: Hides a food's nutrients (shown as ???) until you have eaten it. Eating a meal or pie teaches you each of its ingredients. How filling a food is still shows. The nutrition window only suggests foods you have eaten.
worldattribute-complexnutritionHidePoiso: Part of Discover Nutrition, and only works while that is on. Hides the health a food takes from you, such as a poisonous mushroom's, until you have eaten it once. A little extra danger for braver players.
worldattribute-complexnutritionDiminishi: When on, eating a lot of one thing gives less and less: carbs, fats and protein give fewer calories past a day's worth, and vitamins and minerals count for less past a day's worth eaten at once. Switch it off and every gram counts in full.
worldattribute-complexnutritionWildHarve: How much a wild crop gives when you harvest it, compared with the same crop grown on farmland. A wild spelt plant gives about 1 or 2 grain at 25% (vanilla), 2 to 4 at 50%, and as much as a farmed one (5 to 7) at 100%. Seeds are not affected.
worldattribute-complexnutritionMaxFullne: How much a character's stomach holds, in fullness. 300 is about 1 kilogram of food. Fullness always empties at a rate of 100 an hour and only decides how much you can eat at once. 0 means no limit.
worldattribute-complexnutritionEffects-d: When on, your vitamin and mineral stores change how your character performs. A well-stocked store gives a bonus, such as better aim, faster mining or more health, and an empty one a penalty. Each nutrient's effect can also be switched off on its own on the World Settings tab of the settings menu.
